newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures up on gains in CBOT project A.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures up on gains in CBOT project A.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures reversed early losses to settle higher across the board on Monday, on animated buying in the afternoon session, supported by gains in CBOT project A trading, traders said.
Prices ranged from 190 yen to 460 yen per tonne higher, with benchmark March contract ending up 190 yen at 16,600 yen.
The daily volume was estimated at 56,839 lots.
Prices started lower, but the higher CBOT project A trading spurred buying in nearby months, which spilled over in other contracts in the afternoon session.
A higher Chicago wheat market last Friday also supported sentiment here. "The Chicago corn market is likely to be hauled up by the bullish Chicago wheat market," one trader said.

On CBOT Project A, the spot May corn contract was traded at $3.05 per bushel at 0823 GMT, up from $2.99-1/2 at Friday's close. Spot May CBOT soybean futures were traded at $8.44-1/4 per bushel on the overnight trading system, up from $8.30-1/2 at Friday's close.
"Prices on CBOT Project A, particularly soybean futures rebounded strongly in a correction of oversold conditions last Friday," one trader said.
